notes: Samma Jams bore Islamic laqabs and the title Sultan (Digby). Arghuns were Timurid amirs from Kandahar; Shah Beg moved into Sind (Iranica); Met list dates Arghun rule 1520-1591 among Sultanate dynasties. Both Muslim, Persianate.

source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Ethiopia: The Zagwe and Solomonic dynasties - https://www.britannica.com/place/Ethiopia/The-Zagwe-and-Solomonic-dynasties
notes: Ifat, a Muslim state, made tributary by Amda Tseyon in 1328 and annexed by Yeshaq I c. 1415. Solomonic monarchs were heads of the Christian church and sponsored theological works; chronicles and hymns of Amda Tseyon's reign attest writing.

source2: Marco Demichelis, The Oromo and the Historical Process of Islamisation of Ethiopia (book chapter, c. 2016) - https://www.academia.edu/32925374/The_Oromo_and_the_Historical_process_of_Islamisation_of_Ethiopia
notes: 16th-century Oromo expansion (gada groups, no dynasty) overran Hadiya. Britannica: southern Oromo (Arsi, Borana) remained sky-god worshippers. Demichelis inconsistent: gradual Islamisation from 16th c. near Harar, but Arsi-Bale kept awama. Oral culture; writing inferred N.

source1: Philadelphia Museum of Art, The Book of War: The Free Library of Philadelphia's Mughal Razmnama Folios - https://www.philamuseum.org/exhibitions/the-book-of-war-the-free-library-of-philadelphias-mughal-razmnama-folios

notes: Humayun regained Agra and Delhi 1555. Akbar, a Muslim ruler, set up a Sanskrit translation bureau (1574), commissioned the Mahabharata translation, held interfaith debates with Hindus; 1582 new religious code. Patronage alongside Islam, not conversion.

source1: Etienne de la Vaissiere, KUSHANSHAHS i. History, Encyclopaedia Iranica, 2016 - http://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/kushanshahs-01
source2: A. Shapur Shahbazi, HORMOZD KUSANSAH, Encyclopaedia Iranica - http://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/hormozd-kusansah
notes: Kushanshahs styled themselves Mazdean lord, fire-altar coin types; kept Oesho/Shiva imagery; no royal Buddhist patronage attested. Bactrian and Pahlavi inscriptions. Kushan population religiously mixed (Buddhist, Iranian, Saiva); database Buddhism kept.

source2: Mary Boyce, Achaemenid Religion, Encyclopaedia Iranica, 1983 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/achaemenid-religion
notes: Artaxerxes III reconquered Egypt 343; temples plundered, Apis reportedly killed (Britannica). Second Persian domination ended 332 (Bresciani, Iranica EGYPT i). Boyce: later Achaemenids Zoroastrian (debated). Earlier Darius I temple patronage predates this conquest.

source1: Venetia Ann Porter, The History and Monuments of the Tahirid Dynasty of the Yemen 858-923/1454-1517, PhD thesis, Durham University, 1992 - https://etheses.durham.ac.uk/id/eprint/1558/1/1558_v1.pdf
notes: Porter: Tahirids an indigenous Sunni (Shafi'i) Yemeni dynasty, ended abruptly when defeated by a small Mamluk force with firearms in 1517. Britannica: Mamluk Egypt a centre of Sunni scholarship.

notes: Corrected database Christianity: Seid Ahmed (citing Lange, Orent) says Kafa's indigenous religion mobilised resistance; after 1897 it was disrupted and Christian proselytizing expanded. Earlier Christianity was nominal or faded. Menelik's Orthodox court kept its faith.

source2: C. E. Bosworth, GHURIDS, Encyclopaedia Iranica, 2001 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ghurids
notes: Gahadavala state rested on Brahmanical ideology; Jayachandra killed at Chandawar fighting Muhammad of Ghur (c. 1194). Ghurids strong upholders of Sunni Islam, Persian literary patrons; Aybak built Quwwat al-Islam mosque. No Hindu adoption.

Ayyubids under Turan Shah, Saladin's brother, conquered Yemen 1173-74 (Britannica Zabid). Ayyubids were a zealous Sunni dynasty; Yemen's prior rulers were Muslim (Zaydi, Ismaili Sulayhids/Zurayids, Mahdids).
